title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 72 with ampicillin already in the regimen

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved Batch A as presented ("yeah they look fine", #218); the owner did not report reading the sources.

story: A 72-year-old woman, not immunocompromised, presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 hours, ampicillin 2 g every 4 hours and dexamethasone (with or before the first antibiotic dose) are started; cultures are pending. She has hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV as needed for headache; no laxative is ordered.

prescriptions.instructions: Loading dose then 15 to 20 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours, pharmacy to dose
0.15 mg/kg (10 mg) IV every 6 hours, first dose with or before the first antibiotic dose
0.5 mg IV every 3 hours as needed for headache

expected_findings.summary: Hydromorphone as needed for headache with no stimulant or osmotic laxative ordered.

reference_answer: No intervention: the empiric regimen covers Listeria (age over 50). Continue dexamethasone only if pneumococcal; narrow when cultures return. Add a bowel regimen with the hydromorphone (senna or polyethylene glycol) once she can take it by mouth.
rationale: Negative control for the Listeria rule: ampicillin in the regimen must keep it silent. Case library v2 (#217): the silent Listeria question stays; the bowel regimen finding is added.
